newsitem.title: UK: North Sea wet buyers at standoff as outright jumps.
newsitem.headline: North Sea wet buyers at standoff as outright jumps.

text.p: North Sea physical crude markets saw light action as outright levels jumped up and backwardation blew out.
Sellers of remaining September barrels looked for firmer premiums in the main but potential buyers looked for reduced levels following recent deals.
Dated Brent was assessed doable around Oct -10 cents, up from trade Tuesday at -17 cents, though no deals were reported.
"We need to get a better premium than on Tuesday because the backwardation has blown out, but the sellers won't come up to us, so we could have a quiet day," said one major seller.
IPE October Brent crude gained some 73 cents to trade at $23.61 a barrel at 1545 GMT.

Prices rose as tension increased after Iraq fired missiles at U.S. jets and the U.S. moved B-52 bombers to a base in the Indian Ocean to back its threat of new strikes against Iraq, U.S. defence officals said.
Intermonth spreads gained ground with Oct/Nov trading as high as +73 cents and now assessed at 73/76 cents, while Nov/Dec and Dec/Jan talked 64/70 cents.
Two Brent cargoes were passing through the paper chains today.
Equity holders said they did not expect Norwegian October crude loading programmes until Friday, while Brent could emerge early on Monday.
The Med was subdued as refiners tried to digest higher prices after a flurry of activity earlier in the week.
"After such a price rise, there is always a pause to see if it is safe to buy at the top end of the market," a European refiner said.
He said Urals was relatively tight even beyond September 20 loading dates and there were not too many Iranian cargoes seen offered.
